steps.what: Design robotic systems around material behaviour, throughput, precision and operational constraints

tasks.design: Retain system design with the engineer in the robotic design and simulation environment {OTHER}. Native modelling assists exploration, but repeatable automated design has not been established for the varied material and precision constraints.
tasks.previous_blocker: System architecture depends on interactions among products, tooling, sensing and production flow.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing modelling tools support engineering exploration without replacing it.
tasks.still_hard: A simulated throughput improvement may fail with actual material variability.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer selects architectures and tests the assumptions behind them.
tasks.altitude: No assumed change in design effort or decision rights.

reach.learn: Translate observed variation into design requirements.

evidence.claim: Ansys SimAI predicts designs from past simulations; that capability alone does not establish correct high-throughput robotic architecture.

assumptions: Boundary is engineering design, excluding physical commissioning and separately counted documentation.
OTHER means robotic design and simulation environment. Engineer investigates material behaviour and requirements during s1; no ready-made feasibility flags are assumed.
Consider native design features first. Zero incremental upkeep because no new system or capture workflow is proposed.
research_questions: Which recurring design subproblem has stable constraints and independently checkable results?

already_counted.description: Engineering investigation and design remain fully counted.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gross=0 net=0. Existing simulation runtime is not human labour and no design judgement is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write ad hoc robotic algorithms and code

steps.what: Specify application behaviour, interfaces, failure responses and independently derived test expectations
Write programming code for the specified robotic application in the development environment

loop.purpose: Draft a limited application module from the engineer's specification.
loop.input: Implementation brief and versioned controller documentation.
loop.output: Candidate code with requirement links and stated assumptions.
loop.check: Engineer traces each requirement to code, verifies interface semantics and checks independently specified fault responses and test expectations.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; unsupported interfaces or failed checks return to manual implementation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Try native function blocks first; genuinely ad hoc control logic does not fit fixed templates.

steps.what: Validate algorithms and code in controlled tests before accepting the development revision

tasks.design: Try native blocks in the robot development environment {OTHER}, then use a bounded drafting loop for the remaining ad hoc module. The engineer reviews semantics and independently validates behaviour; {DOCS} holds the implementation brief and accepted revision references.
tasks.previous_blocker: Ad hoc application logic requires manual translation of behaviour and interfaces into code.
tasks.enabler_now: Code drafting can assist this translation when supplied with explicit requirements and checked documentation.
tasks.still_hard: Compiling code does not establish timing correctness or safe physical behaviour.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer defines expected behaviour and accepts only independently checked results.
tasks.altitude: Some first-pass implementation time can shift to validation without changing deployment rights.

reach.learn: Prepare reproducible tests and distinguish implementation defects from equipment faults.

evidence.claim: Siemens Industrial Copilot drafts PLC code and HMI screens; that supports a limited drafting capability, not autonomous robotics deployment.
The robotics module workflow and savings are model knowledge, not measured effects of the cited product.

assumptions: Boundary ends at a validated development revision; production release and separately scoped debugging are excluded.

In s1 the engineer produces requirement IDs, state transitions, units, interfaces, controller version, timing bounds, prohibited actions, fault responses and independently derived expected tests. Capture and verification remain fully counted; gaps require manual specification before drafting.
OTHER means robot development environment. Native libraries precede model drafting; no model writes directly to operational robots.
research_questions: Does blind comparison find semantic defects earlier than manual implementation without increasing validation effort?

already_counted.description: Candidate code review and correction within implementation.

incremental.description: Maintain checked interface examples and evaluate drafting changes.
Development administrator maintains isolated tooling and access.

approvals.approved_version: Exact source hash, controller configuration and validation report; any edit voids acceptance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=86 gross=14 net=7 after 7 upkeep. Zero if unsupported controller semantics force manual coding; 2 for a small supported module with unchanged validation.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Produce device lists and timing charts

steps.what: Reconcile device specifications and event timing assumptions against the current system design
Make device lists and event timing charts from the reconciled register
Check list completeness and chart sequencing before accepting the document revision

tasks.design: Configure {SPREADSHEET} tables and chart templates to render the engineer's reconciled register. Keep engineering completeness and sequence checks in {DOCS} before accepting a revision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Device rows and timing diagrams were repeatedly transcribed and formatted.
tasks.enabler_now: Native tables and chart templates can derive both outputs from explicit records.
tasks.still_hard: Missing devices and incorrect timing assumptions remain engineering errors.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer checks whether the represented sequence matches the real application.
tasks.altitude: Less document construction; system design authority stays unchanged.

reach.learn: Maintain device identifiers and revision correspondence.

evidence.claim: Generating lists and timing charts from structured engineering records is model knowledge; no robotics labour result is cited.

assumptions: Boundary is producing documentation from an existing design, excluding device selection and sequence design.

Engineer produces device IDs, type, location, interface, configuration revision, event IDs, predecessors, start offsets, durations, units and source references in s1. All capture and reconciliation are counted; unresolved timings remain manual and are not plotted as facts.
Test native table and chart configuration before custom rendering code.
research_questions: Do independent checks find every omitted device and overlapping prohibited event?

already_counted.description: Source reconciliation and final engineering review.

approvals.approved_version: Exact source register, device list and timing chart revisions; changes void acceptance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=60 gross=40 net=33 after 7 upkeep. Zero if native documents are already generated; 7 if only recurring formatting and transcription are removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Design or program robotics for clean-up while investigating hazards, containment and failure behaviour

tasks.design: Keep hazardous clean-up engineering with the engineer using the robotic development and simulation environment {OTHER}. Native modelling supports investigation, while site-specific exposure and containment decisions remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Unknown contamination and failure consequences make application design site-dependent.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing modelling can inform options but does not establish suitability for actual hazards.
tasks.still_hard: The robot itself can spread contamination or fail in inaccessible conditions.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer reasons about failure modes and seeks specialist hazard assessment.
tasks.altitude: No assumed reduction in design investigation or change in operational authority.

reach.learn: Translate exposure and containment constraints into robot requirements.

evidence.claim: Retaining site-specific hazardous robotics design is model knowledge; no task-specific measured saving is asserted.

assumptions: Boundary covers design and programming investigation; site authorisation, deployment and clean-up operations are separate and receive no savings.
OTHER means robotic development and simulation environment. Engineer investigates and records hazard assumptions in s1; no free structured hazard classification or safety acceptance is assumed.
Consider existing native simulation first. Zero incremental upkeep because no additional automated workflow is introduced.
research_questions: Which design assumptions can be independently tested without exposing workers or spreading contamination?

already_counted.description: Engineering design and hazard reasoning remain counted.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gross=0 net=0. Site-specific hazardous design is retained without claiming generic simulation speed as labour savings.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Repeated engineering documents can become derived outputs while design and physical validation remain accountable work.
reach: Coordinate device identifiers with drafters and contamination constraints with environmental engineers.
role.ambitious_version: A robotics engineer who uses checked drafts and derived documents to support stronger engineering tests.
